instructions.question: What feeling does this Czech Facebook comment express: positive (thanks, wishes, praise, delight, wanting the product), negative (complaint, sadness, frustration, insult, sarcastic attack), or neutral (factual, questioning, joking or chatty with no clear feeling)?
instructions.rule: Annotators label the expressed feeling even when the brand is not the target: thanks, congratulations, good wishes, delight and craving a product are positive, while sadness, frustration, complaints and insults to other users are negative. A smiley or :D alone does not make a text positive or negative; it needs a feeling word, thanks, wish, sad emoticon like :( or :(((, or a clear complaint. Questions, requests, suggestions, wished-for tariffs, flat fault reports, banter, teasing jokes, mild irony, hopes ('snad', 'doufám') and promo-style statements are neutral.

neutral.what: Questions, information, requests, suggestions, plain problem reports, user banter, jokes, mild irony and hopes without a clear feeling word.
examples: jak deaktivuji službu Útrata?? (how do I deactivate the Útrata service??)
Chci levnější volání, 3G pokrytí, Internet bez cenzury a bez FUP. (I want cheaper calls, 3G coverage, internet without censorship and without FUP.)
Už mám objednáno =) (I've already ordered)
jen jestli ondra není netbot, na určitý typ otázky vždy stejná odpověď :-D (I wonder if Ondra isn't a netbot, always the same answer to a certain type of question)
neutral.cues: jak (how), proč (why) in plain questions, prosím (please), snad (hopefully), doufám (I hope), kdyby (if), :D in banter
neutral.not_for: Questions loaded with sad or angry markers ('já mám vynulované skore :((((( nevíte proč???' (my score has been reset, does anyone know why???)) are negative.

positive.what: Thanks, congratulations, good wishes, praise of products, ads, animals or photos, delight, loyalty, and wanting or buying the product with enthusiasm.
examples: Díky za odpověď :-) (Thanks for the answer)
Držím pěsti!!! (Fingers crossed!!!)
Dal bych si :P (I'd have some)
Jejda mane,to je micánek :) :) (Oh man, what a kitty)
positive.cues: děkuji, díky (thank you), všechno nejlepší (all the best), držím pěsti (fingers crossed), super, krásné (beautiful), dal bych si (I'd have some), chci taky (I want one too), jůů (yay)
positive.not_for: Factual or chatty lines with only a smiley ('Už je hotový :D' (it's done now :D)), hopes ('snad se v Opavě dočkáme :)' (hopefully we'll get it in Opava)), and promo text are neutral.

negative.what: Complaints about price, service or product, threats to leave, sarcasm or mockery, insults to other users, and sad or frustrated remarks.
examples: Jdu si do trafiky pro simku konkurence, už mě to přestává bavit. (I'm going to get a competitor's SIM, I'm getting fed up.)
zase jsem to nestih, poslední dobou mi skoro pokaždý tyhle bomba akce utečou přímo před očima :-( (I missed it again; lately these great deals nearly always slip away right in front of me)
Chudák kočka,....:-/ (Poor cat)
negative.cues: předražený (overpriced), nefunguje (doesn't work), už nikdy (never again), škoda (pity), chudák (poor thing), ty vole (dude, as a swear), osel (donkey, as an insult), :( , :(((, :-/
negative.not_for: Flat fault reports or questions without frustration markers, and light teasing between users, are neutral.
